threads.topic: Kaspa's 5,700 TPS vs Bitcoin's 7; what real throughput unlocks

tweets.text:
Bitcoin does about 7 transactions per second.

$KAS just hit 5,700.

That's 800x the throughput on a fair-launched proof-of-work chain.

Here's why this number matters more than people realize 🧵
tweets.hook: Bitcoin does about 7 transactions per second.

tweets.text:
Bitcoin's whole reason for existing was to be peer-to-peer electronic cash.

The 2008 white paper is explicit. The pitch was: a payment system that doesn't need banks.

That requires the network to move money at the speed money needs to move.

It doesn't.

7 transactions per second across the entire global network. Confirmation times measured in tens of minutes. Fees that spike to $20+ during congestion.

Try paying for a coffee with that. Try sending payroll to a thousand employees with that.

Now look at $KAS.

5,700 TPS. Block times in milliseconds. Fees that round to zero.

The chain that can actually do what Bitcoin promised in 2008 wasn't built by Satoshi.

It was built by someone who looked at Bitcoin's limits and decided to fix them.

Why throughput matters:

No asset can be money if you can't move it fast enough.

Gold isn't money in the modern sense; it's a settlement layer. Bitcoin is currently in the same category: a slow settlement layer pretending to be money.

5,700 TPS opens doors that Bitcoin physically cannot:

Real merchant adoption. Micropayments. Global remittance flows. On-chain commerce at consumer scale.

These aren't theoretical. They're waiting for a chain that can actually handle them.

The bull case for $KAS isn't "it might replace Bitcoin."

The bull case is: Bitcoin can't do its own job. $KAS can.

When the global payment layer actually needs replacing, the question stops being "which crypto." It becomes "which one actually works at scale."

If this reframed how you're thinking about Bitcoin's TPS limits; there's more where it came from.

threads.topic: October 2025 was a midcycle top, not THE cycle top

tweets.text:
October 2025 wasn't the cycle top.

It was a midcycle top so weak it didn't even reach average power law.

The 2013 and 2019 midcycle tops both blew past it.

Here's what people are mourning that didn't actually happen 🧵
tweets.hook: October 2025 wasn't the cycle top.

tweets.text:
First, definitions.

A midcycle top is the local high partway through a cycle, not the cycle top itself.

In 2013, $BTC ran from ~$13 to ~$259 in Q1, peaked, sold off ~85%, then ran to ~$1,150 by year-end. That early peak was a midcycle top, not the cycle top.

The 2019 setup was the same shape.

$BTC ran from ~$3,200 in December 2018 to ~$13,800 in June 2019. Then it sold off into ~$3,800 by March 2020. Then it printed the actual cycle top at ~$69,000 in November 2021.

June 2019 was a midcycle top. The cycle top came later.

What both midcycle tops have in common: they blew well past average power law.

Average power law isn't a magic level. It's the regression of $BTC's lifetime price drawn through the middle.

Past midcycle tops cleared it convincingly. That's how you tell a real local high from noise.

October 2025 didn't reach it.

The "top" everyone is now mourning peaked below average power law. That's not a cycle top by any prior pattern. It's a local high inside a sideways structure.

If October had even matched the 2019 midcycle overshoot, $BTC would have printed well above $200k.

The four-year cycle zombies grieving October as the top are extrapolating from a midcycle high that didn't even break trend.

It would be like calling June 2019 the top of the 2017–2021 cycle.

Nobody serious did that then. Nobody serious should be doing it now.

The actual cycle top is still ahead.

When it prints, it'll be well above average power law, like every previous one. That's not a guess; it's the pattern every cycle has followed.

If you sold October expecting the bear, you sold a midcycle dip thinking it was a peak.

Power law charts aren't the only thing the four-year cycle crowd is misreading right now.

threads.topic: The four-year cycle was always macro coincidence; dip was self-inflicted
threads.variation_label: B — Macro causal arc with $95k counterfactual payoff

tweets.text:
The four-year cycle didn't break.

It never existed.

What people called "the cycle" was three macro variables happening to line up. And the people still acting like it's real cost $BTC roughly $15k of price right now.

Here's the actual story 🧵
tweets.hook: The four-year cycle didn't break.

tweets.text:
For a decade, three things lined up almost perfectly with the halving calendar:

1. The business cycle (PMI expansion → contraction)
2. Money printing (QE on → QT on)
3. Interest rates (cuts → hikes)

People credited the halving. The halving was incidental.

The proof: every prior crypto bear (2014, 2018, 2022) maps cleanly to PMI rolling over, QE ending, and rates rising.

Not "Bitcoin halved 18 months ago, time for a bear."

The macro environment did the work. The halving narrative just borrowed credit for it.

This time the three variables didn't line up.

PMI: expanding.
QE: running.
Rates: coming down.

The conditions that created every previous "crypto winter" simply aren't present. The macro side of the cycle isn't there.

But the four-year cycle zombies didn't notice.

They saw the calendar (year four after a halving). They saw a shutdown-driven dip. They assumed the bear had arrived.

Long-term holders started distributing into it. Sell pressure compounded. Down we went.

The dip wasn't macro. It wasn't structural.

It was a self-fulfilling prophecy from people convinced of a cycle that never existed.

If they hadn't dumped, $BTC would be at ~$95k right now. The current ~$80k is the cost of acting on a dead theory.

The lesson isn't "the cycle is broken" or "the halving doesn't matter."

The lesson is that "the cycle" was always macro wearing a Bitcoin costume.

Once you see it as macro coincidence, you can't unsee it. And you stop selling when the calendar says "bear."

The four-year cycle had a good run. It's done.

threads.topic: First-ever crypto bear during expansion + QE (pattern break)

tweets.text:
Every previous crypto bear lined up with macro tightening.

Rates up. QT. PMI down.

Either we just rewrote how cycles work, or this isn't a bear at all 🧵
tweets.hook: Every previous crypto bear lined up with macro tightening.

tweets.text:
2014 bear: post-Mt.Gox unwind on the surface.

The deeper story was the Fed taper. QE3 ended December 2014. PMI rolled through 2015.

$BTC drained from ~$1,150 to ~$170. The headlines blamed the exchange collapse. The macro did most of the lifting.

2018 bear: ICO bust on the surface; rate hikes underneath.

The Fed lifted from 1.25% to 2.5% over 12 months. QT ran simultaneously. PMI peaked mid-2018 and rolled.

$BTC went ~$19,500 → ~$3,200.

2022 bear: Luna and FTX dominate the headlines, but the real catalyst was the fastest hiking cycle in 40 years.

The Fed went 0% → 5.5% in 18 months. QT was running. PMI contracted.

$BTC: ~$69,000 → ~$15,500. The collapses were symptoms.

Three bears. Three different surface stories (Mt.Gox, ICO bust, Luna/FTX).

One identical macro setup underneath: tightening + contraction.

That's the actual playbook. The thing people called "the four-year cycle" was just the macro cycle.

Now look at the present.

PMI: expanding.
QE: running.
Rates: coming down, not up.

Pull a chart of any prior crypto bear and overlay these conditions. They don't fit. None of the boxes that defined the past three bears are checked.

So either:

1. We just witnessed the first crypto bear in history that happened during the opposite macro setup, OR
2. What looked like a bear was actually a panic in a bull setup, driven by people still acting on the old playbook.

Occam's razor picks the second one.

The macro behind crypto is doing the opposite of what most accounts will admit.

threads.topic: 50-week SMA breakdown was belief, not structure; LTH dumping at the bottom

tweets.text:
The 50-week SMA breakdown wasn't real.

200-week SMA was barely wicked on a single Thursday. No weekly close at or below it.

Technically, this isn't even crypto winter. People behaved like it was.

Here's the cost of acting on belief instead of charts 🧵
tweets.hook: The 50-week SMA breakdown wasn't real.

tweets.text:
"Crypto winter" has a definition.

It's the period after $BTC closes weekly below the 200-week SMA, traditionally for sustained weeks.

The 200-week SMA is the long-term trend line. Closing below it is what "the long-term structure broke" actually means in chart terms.

What actually happened in October:

$BTC wicked toward the 200-week SMA on a single Thursday. It didn't close at or below it on the weekly. Not even once.

By the strict definition, the structural break never happened. The trend held.

But people behaved as if the break had happened.

Long-term holders, the cohort that's supposed to weather these moments, distributed into the dip instead of accumulating.

The on-chain data is unambiguous: LTH supply dropped through October and November.

Ill-advised long-term holders sold a bear they invented.

Not because the chart broke. Because they thought it would.

The four-year cycle calendar said "year four = bear." The dip felt like confirmation. Down went the bags.

The cost of that behavior:

$BTC at ~$80k instead of ~$95k.

That ~$15k delta is a tax on people who acted on a thesis their own charts weren't confirming. It's also a discount for whoever didn't sell.

The lesson is small and uncomfortable:

Read your own charts before you act.

The 50-week SMA "breakdown" wasn't a breakdown. The 200-week SMA "test" wasn't a structural break. Crypto winter wasn't here.

It was always belief acting on incomplete reading.

Most accounts will keep telling you what the chart "feels like."

threads.topic: US Bitcoin Strategic Reserve = instant new ATH

tweets.text:
The day the US announces it's buying $BTC for a strategic reserve, every chart you're using becomes obsolete.

A sovereign buyer of last resort changes the math.

Here's what that announcement does, who's already done it, and how to position 🧵
tweets.hook: The day the US announces it's buying $BTC for a strategic reserve, every chart you're using becomes obsolete.

tweets.text:
First, why does this single announcement re-price the entire market in minutes?

Because the US is the issuer of the world reserve currency. When a sovereign of that size publicly commits to a buy program, every other holder has to immediately mark up their cost-basis estimate.

If the US is bidding, the floor is now wherever the US is willing to bid.

There's no precedent for what that does to price discovery.

The closest analogs are when central banks have publicly committed to gold accumulation. Those happened against a multi-trillion-dollar gold market.

Bitcoin's entire market cap is smaller than the US gold reserve at market value.

Second, the precedents. This isn't theoretical anymore.

El Salvador has been actively buying $BTC since 2021 (a 1-BTC-daily program among other purchases).

Bhutan accumulated sovereign $BTC reserves through state-owned mining since around 2019, with disclosed reserves north of $750M.

At the state level: Texas signed strategic Bitcoin reserve legislation in 2025. New Hampshire passed similar legislation. Several other states have introduced bills.

The pattern is clear. Sovereigns are quietly building positions before the federal level commits.

Third, the asymmetry.

If the US announces, $BTC re-prices instantly to a number that includes the implied future demand.

If the US doesn't announce, $BTC stays roughly where it is.

Limited downside. Asymmetric upside. This is why I'm not selling into rallies right now.

Fourth, the timeline.

The current US holdings (~200K $BTC from seizures) are already designated as a strategic reserve under the March 2025 executive order.

The next step is whether the Treasury announces an active acquisition program. Reports suggest it could land within weeks.

That announcement is the unlock.

threads.topic: Bear market is the real test (Lab 98x update)

A bull market makes every project look strong. Liquidity is everywhere; even projects with no fundamentals print 50-100x because retail throws capital at anything that moves.

A bear market does the opposite. It filters by survival.

My 3-question filter.

Question 2: Are they still getting CEX listings?

CEX listings cost money and effort. Teams that keep landing them during a bear are signaling commitment from operators, not just punters.

Quiet on listings = quiet on the project.

Question 3: Are they still shipping product or content?

Devs and founders who keep building during a bear demonstrate they were never just pumping for the rotation.

Teams that go quiet on product or social are flagging that they were here for the cycle, not the chain.

Third, Lab as proof.

Lab launched in October 2025. I called it on day two of launch at 10 cents. We swing-traded it back in at 7.7 cents in December. It just hit 98x.

That's 98x in a bear market. Not in the next rally. Right now, while four-year cycle zombies are still calling for further downside.

threads.topic: The 90/10 wealth transfer (the dumpers paid the holders)

tweets.text:
In every bear market, 90% of holders transfer wealth to 10% of holders.

The dumpers create the discount. The accumulators take it.

The Oct/Nov dip was the cleanest example we've ever seen. Here's what 90/10 actually looked like
tweets.hook: In every bear market, 90% of holders transfer wealth to 10% of holders.

Bear markets are not random price events. They are wealth transfers.

The supply of coins doesn't change. The number of holders doesn't change much. What changes is the distribution: who holds what coins, at what cost basis. Every bear, that distribution shifts dramatically.

The four-year cycle zombies dumped. Long-term holders distributed (the on-chain data is unambiguous). Retail panicked.

Whoever didn't sell got the discount.

Every bear is a wealth transfer because every bear is fundamentally a coordination failure.

People who would have been better off holding sell anyway, because their information environment tells them the asset is going lower.

If you held through October and November, you're already on the 10 side. Stay there.
